segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are testifying about yourself; your testimony is not true.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Even if I do testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You judge by human standards; I judge no one.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet even if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone—it is I and the Father who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two people is true.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where is your father?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spoke these words in the treasury while teaching in the temple, and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He is not going to kill himself, is he, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: That is why I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why do I speak to you at all?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have much to say about you and much to judge, but the one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him I speak to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but speak these things just as the Father taught me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the one who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was saying these things, many believed in him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are Abraham’s descendants and have never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The slave does not remain in the household forever; the son remains forever.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will really be free.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know that you are Abraham’s descendants. Yet you are seeking to kill me, because my word finds no room in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I speak what I have seen in my Father’s presence, and you, then, do what you have heard from your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Our father is Abraham.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you are Abraham’s children, you would be doing the works of Abraham.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are doing the works of your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father—God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and am here. I have not come on my own; he sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Why do you not understand what I am saying? Because you cannot hear my word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are from your father the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar and the father of lies.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is from God hears the words of God. This is why you do not hear: because you are not from God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are we not right to say that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I do not have a demon. I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it, and he judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever keeps my word will never see death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never taste death.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Surely you are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who do you make yourself out to be?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet you have not come to know him, but I know him. If I were to say that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Your father Abraham was overjoyed that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, before Abraham was born, I am.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid and went out of the temple.

notes.phrase: Then Jesus spoke to them again
notes.note: Verses 1–11 of this chapter belong to the story of the woman caught in adultery (7:53–8:11). That passage is missing from the earliest manuscripts and appears at different places in later ones, and most scholars judge that it was not originally part of this Gospel. Without it, verse 12 continues directly from the debate in the temple at the end of chapter 7.

The setting is still the Feast of Tabernacles (7:2, 37). Later rabbinic tradition describes great lamps lit in the temple’s Court of Women during that festival, the area where the treasury of verse 20 is usually located. Many interpreters hear the saying against that backdrop, though John does not mention the lamps.

The Greek is literally “according to the flesh.” Here “flesh” means the merely human point of view—judging by appearances and human criteria—not the body or sinful desire. Several modern versions render it the same way.

notes.phrase: the testimony of two people is true
notes.note: The rule that a matter must be established by two or three witnesses comes from Deuteronomy 17:6 and 19:15. “True” here carries the legal sense “valid,” as in verses 13 and 14. Jesus names himself and the Father as the two witnesses.

The Greek is simply “I am” (egō eimi) with nothing after it, which is why the hearers ask “Who are you?” in the next verse. In everyday Greek the phrase can mean “I am he” or “it is I,” and it is rendered that way here and in verse 28; it also echoes God’s self-declaration in the Greek version of Isaiah (for example 43:10). The same two words stand in verse 58, where nothing can be supplied and the rendering is “I am.”

notes.phrase: Why do I speak to you at all?
notes.traditional: Just what I have been telling you from the beginning
notes.note: This is one of the most disputed sentences in John. The traditional rendering takes the opening phrase as “from the beginning,” but used adverbially it often means “at all,” John elsewhere uses a different expression for “from the beginning,” and the verb is in the present tense. The Greek edition translated here punctuates the sentence as a question, and ancient Greek-speaking commentators read it as an expression of exasperation. Many scholars and most English versions still prefer the traditional sense.
The verb means both to raise physically and to exalt. John uses it for Jesus being raised on the cross, which is at the same time his exaltation (3:14; 12:32–33). “Lifted up” keeps both senses.

notes.phrase: the Jews who had believed him
notes.note: These hearers are said to have believed him, yet in the verses that follow the audience is said to be seeking to kill him. Some interpreters think their belief was shallow and gives way under challenge. Others think the group addressed widens again to the hostile crowd of the earlier verses. The text does not settle the question.

notes.phrase: does not remain in the household forever
notes.traditional: does not remain in the house forever
notes.note: The Greek idiom, literally “into the age,” usually means “never” when it follows a negative, as in verses 51 and 52. Here the contrast with the son who “remains forever” shows that the sense is “not permanently” rather than “never”: a slave has no lasting place in the household, and a son does.

notes.phrase: do what you have heard from your father
notes.traditional: you do what you have heard from your father
notes.note: The Greek has simply “the father” in both halves of the verse, and the verb “do” can be a statement or a command. The rendering here takes it as a contrast between two fathers, anticipating verses 41 and 44, as most English versions do. The alternative is an appeal: “so you too should do what you have heard from the Father.” Some manuscripts add “my” and “your” to make the contrast explicit.

The word covers unlawful sexual relations in general. In the prophets it is also a standing image for idolatry—Hosea speaks of “children of whoredom”—which fits the reply “We have one Father—God”: the speakers claim to be faithful Israel, not children of a false god. Some interpreters also hear in the emphatic “We” a slur on the circumstances of Jesus’s own birth, but this is uncertain.

notes.phrase: You are from your father the devil
notes.note: This is said within a dispute among Jews, to the particular hearers who, Jesus says, are seeking to kill him (verses 37 and 40). He has already granted that they are Abraham’s descendants; the argument is that conduct, not ancestry, shows whose child a person is. The verse was later turned against the Jewish people as a whole, a use the context does not support.

These are the same two Greek words as in verses 24 and 28, here with nothing that could be supplied after them and set against Abraham’s coming into existence. Most interpreters hear an echo of God’s self-declarations in Isaiah, and many also connect it with the divine name in Exodus 3:14. The attempt at stoning in the next verse suggests the hearers took it as blasphemy.

candidates.reason: A key Johannine term rendered variously as “abide,” “remain,” “continue” or “stay”; readers lose the thread across John and 1 John if it varies.

candidates.rendering: human standards (in the phrase κατὰ τὴν σάρκα)
candidates.reason: “Flesh” has several distinct senses across the Gospels and Paul, and the phrase κατὰ σάρκα recurs often enough to need a fixed policy on when to keep “flesh.”
Translations split between “slave” and “servant” throughout the New Testament, and the choice changes how readers hear both parables and Paul’s self-descriptions.
Rendered “fornication,” “sexual immorality,” “unchastity” or “prostitution” in different versions, with a metaphorical idolatry sense that also needs a consistent approach.
“Seed,” “offspring” and “descendants” are all in use, and Paul’s argument in Galatians 3 turns on the singular, so one policy is needed across books.
